2026_10_NE_DET.headline: Right side, for a reason the model couldn't see. Maye's first-quarter injury decided the game and the total.
right: The lean was Detroit. The model had DET by 3.3 against a 2.5 line, and Detroit covered by 22.5.
Jared Goff's 303 passing yards were close to his 262 projection, and it was a normal game for him (he's averaged 267).
wrong: The over lean (model 51.6, line 51) lost. The final total was 45.

Jahmyr Gibbs had 252 yards against a projection of 116 (88 rushing, 29 receiving). Detroit led 21-3 at halftime and kept him on the field. The model doesn't push a back's touches up when it expects his team to be ahead, and this game didn't even look one-sided before kickoff.
chance: Drake Maye got hurt on a sack with 9:43 left in the first quarter, after 5 dropbacks. Tommy DeVito threw 25 of New England's 33 passes. This is the main reason the result went so far from both the model's number and the market's.
Fumble bounces: New England fumbled once and got it back. Detroit fumbled none. That's about 1.6 points in New England's favour, so it doesn't change the read.
The Detroit side covered, but no pregame number had them winning by 25. Don't count this one as a win for the model's read.
improve: Maye's 48 yards (projected 260) and the receivers' collapse under DeVito are counted in the week's projection misses. Leaving out games where a starter left early, as the floors already do, would keep the miss averages from being skewed by injuries.
Worth a pre-set test: give a lead back extra carries when his team is a big favourite in the second half. This game alone isn't evidence. It's a question for the backtest.

2026_10_MIA_IND.headline: Both leans were close calls. Miami played slightly better, Indianapolis got the bounces, and two defensive touchdowns carried the over.
right: The model's total (43.3) was much closer to the 46 final than the market's 38. It leaned over and won.
Miami's offense under Kyle McCord came in close to the projections, with Caleb Douglas at 71 yards (49 projected).
wrong: The model had Indianapolis by 6.9 against a 4.5 line. Indianapolis won by 2. Miami had more successful plays (38% of plays to 35%) and a better EPA per play (−0.09 to −0.15).
Daniel Jones threw for 108 yards (190 projected), tying his season low, and Tyler Warren caught 1 yard (45 projected). The model trusted Indianapolis's passing game more than this game supported.
chance: Two non-offensive touchdowns, one each way: an Indianapolis strip-sack fumble return in the third quarter and a Miami 59-yard pick-six six minutes later. Without those 14 points the total is 32, an under.

Fumble bounces favoured Indianapolis by about 5 points (2 fumbles, 0 lost; Miami 1 fumble, 1 lost). With even bounces, Miami wins by about 3. The spread lean lost even with that help, so the miss on the side was real.
So the over win was mostly chance. The side loss was a model miss, not bad luck.
improve: When a team starts a new quarterback, check how much the model moved its number. Here it lowered Miami (McCord −0.13) and still made Indianapolis too big a favourite. This is the kind of game the uncertain-quarterback test (Nov 11) covers. Adding it to that test's sample would help.

2026_10_SF_DAL.headline: 86 points against a 56 total. Nothing in the pregame numbers pointed to a shootout like this. The over lean won, but with a thin edge.
right: The over lean (model 57.6, line 56) won easily, but a 1.6-point lean isn't what won it. Read this as a coin flip that landed the right way.
The model's side read was right that the game would be closer than the line. San Francisco won by 6 and the model had them by 0.9. The line was 4, so the model's lean on Dallas +4 lost by 2.
wrong: Christian McCaffrey: 161 receiving yards on a 36-yard projection. He'd never topped 61 this season. Brock Purdy threw for 389 (257 projected). San Francisco gained 0.51 EPA per play, its best game of the season.
Dallas's pass game beat projections too: Dak Prescott 343 yards (261), George Pickens 145 (64). Both defenses played far below their ratings.
chance: Dallas went 4 for 5 on fourth down, kept drives alive and ran 82 plays. That much volume is hard to predict and it pushed the total up.
No defensive or return touchdowns and no short missed field goals. The points came from offenses, not bounces.
improve: Nothing to fix from one game. Both the model and the market missed by about 30. Keep an eye on whether San Francisco's defense holds up next week. If its rating keeps lagging what it gives up, that's a rating-speed question for the backtest, not a reason to change anything now.

right: The model had the margin at CIN by 3.1 against a 3.5 line, so it wasn't confident about Pittsburgh, and it doesn't lose much on the read. Neither number saw a 20-point game.
wrong: Pittsburgh's offense went flat: 21% of plays were successful (Cincinnati 63%), 0 for 3 in the red zone, 5 punts in 10 drives. Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 (213 projected), his season low.
